creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Removed functions get golden migration hints while removed syntax dies with misleading parse errors:

| Removed | What the author sees |
|---|---|
| `display` | RAD40008, with a migration URL |
| `get_default` | RAD20028, naming the exact rewrite |
| `string` | "Missing operator between 'what' and 'string'" (RAD10021) |
| `recover:` | "Invalid for loop syntax" (RAD10001) |
| `$!` | doubled "Unexpected '!'" (RAD10009) |

The first two are the model. The review watched the difference play out: RAD40008 made `chimera`'s breakage self-explaining while `arguspush`'s was baffling.

Extend the treatment to `$!`, `recover:`, `unsafe`, and `string`.

---

### Orientation

- Two separate mechanisms produce the two good diagnostics in the table, and neither covers syntax:
  - **Removed functions**: `rts/rl/migrations.go` holds `RemovedFuncHints`, a name-to-hint map with exactly two entries today (`get_default`, `get_stash_dir`). It is read by the runtime at `core/func_helpers.go:91-95` and by the checker, so the two never drift.
  - **Removed block keywords**: `rts/check/ast_checks.go:174-190` (`addDeprecatedBlockKeywordErrors`) walks the AST for `request`/`display` rad blocks and emits `rl.ErrDeprecatedBlockKeyword` (`"40008"`, `rts/rl/errors.go:126`) with the migration URL inline.
- The four targets here - `$!`, `recover:`, `unsafe`, `string` - are **syntax**, so neither mechanism applies. They never reach the AST; they die during parse-error interpretation.

### Where to start

- `rts/check/error_messages.go` is the layer that turns tree-sitter's raw parse failures into Rad diagnostics. It already contains targeted heuristics that replace bare "Unexpected ..." messages with real guidance (see the comments at lines 241, 258, 399, 753). The three bad messages in the card come from this file:
  - `"Missing operator between '%s' and '%s'"` at line 832 (`rl.ErrMissingOperator`, `10021`)
  - `"Invalid for loop syntax"` at line 979 (`rl.ErrInvalidSyntax`, `10001`)
  - `"Unexpected '%s'"` at line 990 (`rl.ErrUnexpectedToken`, `10009`)
  Add detections next to these, following the existing heuristics' shape.
- The removal record for three of the four is `docs-web/docs/releases.md:492-520` (v0.6.12), which lists the old/new pairs verbatim: `$!` cmd -> `$` cmd (critical by default), `unsafe $` cmd -> `$` cmd `catch:`, `recover:` -> `catch:`.
- `string` has **no** removal record anywhere in the repo - not in `releases.md`, not in `SYNTAX.md`, not in any migration guide. Establish through `git log` what it was and when it went before writing a hint for it; do not guess.
- New codes go in `rts/rl/errors.go`, **1xxxx band** (syntax). Never reuse a number; retired codes keep theirs with a `_retired` suffix. Each new code needs `core/error_docs/<code>.md` (style guide: `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`).

### How to verify

```sh
make build
./bin/radd bad-syntax.rad          # eyeball the message before snapshotting it
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=misc/migration
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=errors
go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=parser_errors
make test
```

Existing coverage: `core/testing/snapshots/misc/migration.snap` (end-to-end migration diagnostics) and `rts/check/snapshots/parser_errors/` (checker-level parse errors). Put the case wherever the detection lives.

### Done when

- Each of `$!`, `recover:`, `unsafe`, and `string` produces a diagnostic that names the removed construct and the replacement, matching the quality bar of the `display` and `get_default` messages.
- Every new code has `core/error_docs/<code>.md` with a before/after example, and `rad docs RAD<code>` renders it.
- Snapshot cases exist for all four.
- `make generate` committed - error docs feed the generated `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/`.

### Watch out for

The migration-URL convention (`https://amterp.dev/rad/migrations/v0.X/`) has no page to point at for these. `docs-web/docs/migrations/` contains only `index.md`, `v0.7.md`, `v0.8.md`, `v0.9.md` - and `$!`/`unsafe`/`recover:` were removed in **v0.6.12**, before the guides start. Either backfill a `v0.6.md` (and add it to the nav in `docs-web/mkdocs.yml`, which lists the migration pages explicitly) or point at `migrations/index.md`. Do not emit a URL that 404s - a dead link is worse than the current bad message.

Code snippets in `docs-web/docs/**` are executed by `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go`, so a new migration page with a broken example fails the suite. Per-snippet escape hatches live in `core/testing/docs_snippet_tolerances.go`.
title: Extend migration hints to the syntax that still dies badly
